question: A 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician because she has not yet had her 1st period. She was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery. She is up to date on all vaccines and meeting all developmental milestones. She has no history of a serious illness and takes no medications. Physical examination shows underdeveloped breasts with scant pubic and axillary hair. Speculum examination shows a short vagina and no cervix. The remainder of the physical examination shows no abnormalities. Pelvic ultrasound shows no uterus. Which of the following is the most likely karyotype in this patient?
analysis: The clinical presentation of the 16-year-old girl suggests a condition known as Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome, characterized by the absence of a uterus and cervix, underdeveloped secondary sexual characteristics, and primary amenorrhea. The most common karyotype associated with MRKH syndrome is 46,XX, indicating that the individual has two X chromosomes but has a congenital absence of the uterus. Other options such as 45,X (Turner syndrome) or 46,XY (Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome) do not fit the clinical findings as there is no indication of Turner syndrome features or male characteristics. Therefore, the most likely karyotype in this patient is 46,XX.
